notes: There are no footnotes, Quran text or honorific glyphs on pp.033-036. Honorifics such as «رحمه الله», «رضي الله عنهم» and «صلى الله عليه وسلم» are printed as words. p.033: p.032 ends its section with a complete sentence, so the marker has no '+'. The first line «الفقير إلى الله» is a calligraphic paragraph. The # heading is printed «أ.د/ يسري رشدي السيد جبر» with dotted ي in both names, in the heading and in the first body line, although CONVENTIONS §2 and STRUCTURE say p.033 prints «يسرى رشدى». I checked this at 500 dpi and both final ي clearly carry two dots, so I wrote يسري رشدي as printed. p.035 and p.036 continue mid-sentence, so their markers have '+'. Dashes: on p.034 the long dash between words is written as an en dash '–' (U+2013), the printed glyph. On p.036 the dash between the dates «١٤٠٠هـ - ١٩٨٠ م» is written as an ASCII hyphen, following CONVENTIONS §2 for dashes between numbers. Spacing in the p.036 dates was measured from 700 dpi zooms: «١٤٠٠هـ» has no space before هـ, and the second date reads «١٤١٣ هـ ١٢ / ٢/١٩٩٣», with spaces around the first slash and none around the second. On p.033 «٢٥محرم» is printed without a space and is written that way. On p.036 the slash is printed with spaces and «١٤١٣ هـ» has a space.
